dedupe_keys.name: infews msa iowa urban food energy water co simulation framework and dashboard

description: INFEWS-MSA is a co-simulation framework for the food-energy-water system of the Des Moines Metropolitan Statistical Area in Iowa, built for the Iowa Urban Food-Energy-Water Systems project. A single Python entry point, Orchestrator.py, chains three models through file exchange: an agent-based model of farmer land-use decisions across six counties in NetLogo 6.4.0, the SWAT watershed hydrology and crop-yield model (2012 rev. 694) driven by the ABM land use, and an Excel-based life-cycle assessment of energy use, water use and greenhouse gas emissions per scenario and year. It covers 41 named scenarios for 2020 to 2050, and stages can be run, resumed or skipped individually. It was developed by Vishal Muralidharan, Jan Thompson and Baskar Ganapathysubramanian at Iowa State University; the companion INFEWS-MSA-Data release v1.0.0 (Zenodo, 11 July 2026) holds the output data and the Streamlit dashboard. The code is free under the MIT licence and the data under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the SWAT source archive (about 1.2 GB) is not in git and must be obtained separately, SWAT runs use a Windows executable, and the ABM-only LCA mode is an approximation. It suits agent-based analysis of land use, water and energy interactions and coupled model design; a related record is the NBSINFRA agent-based models of nature-based solutions.
